Subject: RTBF process + proof-of-deletion timeline — LumenHealth follow-up

Hi Maria — great speaking with you earlier today, and thanks for the time for the demo. Quick recap and the outstanding items I promised to follow up on from a privacy/data-handling perspective so your security and legal teams have what they need to qualify us: 

1) RTBF / delete request flow: high-level steps we discussed (API-based delete request -> job id returned -> background expunge + audit record). I attached the RTBF checklist and API spec for your initial review (rtbf-checklist-lumenhealth.pdf, delete-api-spec.yaml).

2) Proof-of-deletion: you asked for confirmation artifacts (timestamped audit entry + cryptographic hash). We're able to provide a proof-of-deletion artifact on Hosted/Dedicated that includes an audit entry and a signed hash of the deleted metadata. Details and a sample are in the attachments.

3) Backups & snapshots: clarification needed on retention windows for backups & immutable snapshots. We have standard backup retention and constraints to call out — I asked our security/engineering team to detail the timeline and exceptions below (cc Neha and Marissa).

4) Logging & forensics: default log retention and options for reducing retention for specific customers (we can scope this based on your policy).

5) Data residency & KMS: we support US/EU regions; customer-managed keys available on Dedicated/Private.

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm the security contact who should receive the tech attachments?
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30–45m follow-up with your SecOps + Legal to walk through the deletion SLA and proof-of-deletion artifact.
- We’ll put together a formal POA (implementation plan + timeline + acceptance criteria) once we align on backup constraints.

Thanks — I’ve looped in Neha (engineering/security) and Marissa (legal) to respond to the backup/residency specifics.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 (415) 555-0172
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@lumenhealth.com>

Subject: Re: RTBF process + proof-of-deletion timeline — LumenHealth follow-up

Thanks Diego — good recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Please send the tech docs to our SecOps alias (sec-ops@lumenhealth.com); I’ll loop Legal afterwards.
- For backups: our compliance team requires that any requested permanent deletion include an expunge from backups/snapshots within a defined timeframe. What does Redwood’s timeline look like for expunging backups that may have captured the data as part of daily snapshots or immutable storage?
- For proof-of-deletion we need: (1) a unique request id you can correlate across systems, (2) timestamp, (3) a digest/hash that proves a record existed and was deleted (preferably with a signed attest). Can you confirm the format?
- Also can you share your SOC2 report (redacted) or a security questionnaire?

Appreciate the follow-up — cc’ing sec-ops. They may respond with more detail on the backup SLA they expect.

Best,
Maria Garcia
Director, Platform Security | LumenHealth
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@lumenhealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RTBF process + proof-of-deletion timeline — LumenHealth follow-up

Hi Maria (and Diego) — following up with the technical details that should answer your backup/POI questions. I summarized below and attached a short contract-ready delete API contract and a proof-of-deletion sample artifact for your security review.

Summary (high-level):
- Delete workflow: POST /v1/data/delete { selector } -> 202 Accepted + job_id. Job id can be polled via GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}. Once expunge is complete we emit an audit event and produce a proof-of-deletion artifact that includes: request_id, resource_digest (sha256 over resource metadata), deleted_timestamp (ISO8601), and a Redwood-signed signature block. See proof-of-deletion-sample.txt (attached).

- Primary storage expunge SLA: for Hosted customers, primary storage expunge completes within 48 hours for typical lineage; we can offer a 30-day accelerated SLA (contracted) for enterprise deals to prioritize expunge jobs. For Dedicated/Private deployments, we can offer tighter SLAs and access to the expunge tooling directly.

- Backups & snapshots: important constraints: immutable snapshots and off-host backups may require separate retention policies. Our standard backup retention is 90 days. For Hosted, we cannot guarantee immediate deletion from third-party snapshot vendors earlier than the retention window unless contracted (we do a best-effort purge and can flag snapshot rehydrations so the data is not restored). For Dedicated/Private we can support a shorter agreed retention or a deletion certificate for customer-managed backup systems.

- Proof format and audit trail: we can provide the signed proof-of-deletion artifact (as noted above) plus an audit log bundle (JSONL) that shows timeline of job state transitions, operator ids, and hashes. Proofs are cryptographically signed with our HSM key; for Dedicated/Private we can sign with a customer-managed KMS where requested.

- Logs retention: default 180 days; can be reduced to 90 days for scoped customers (requires config change + legal appendix).

Action items / proposed POA: 
1) We’ll provide a draft delete API contract and proof artifact (attached).
2) Redwood engineering to validate concrete backup scenarios you provide (e.g., lookback windows, snapshot cadence) — we’ll need sample identifiers or a brief description.
3) Security sync: propose an M+1 day meeting with SecOps and our security/engineering — 30–45m to walk artifacts and acceptance criteria.
4) Contract appendix: Marissa (cc) will draft deletion appendix language and a 30-day/90-day backup option for you to consider.

Attachments: delete-api-contract.json, proof-of-deletion-sample.txt

If you want, we can also scaffold a short integration test plan that triggers a delete on a synthetic record and shares the proof-of-deletion end-to-end with your SecOps team.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
